AdminBootstrapRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /sources/admin_bootstrap``.

Bot sends the calling Telegram user's id + handle. The route
validates the id is in ``Settings.telegram_admin_chat_ids`` and
400s otherwise (admins-only).
AdminBootstrapRequest.title: AdminBootstrapRequest

AdminBootstrapResponse.description:
Response: opaque ``source_id`` + display-name prompt hint.

Mirrors ``RedeemInviteResponse`` so the bot's caller can reuse its
onboarding state machine. ``display_name_prompt`` is True iff a
brand-new admin row was created without a display name set.
AdminBootstrapResponse.title: AdminBootstrapResponse

AssetCandidateDTO.description:
One row in the response to ``GET /assets/search``.

Mirrors the domain ``AssetCandidate`` shape but lives in
``contracts`` because Pydantic is forbidden in ``domain``.

``current_price_usd`` and ``market_cap_usd`` let the bot
differentiate look-alike candidates (distinct ``coingecko_id``s
that share ``(symbol, name)``) by surfacing price + market cap in
the picker body. Both nullable so long-tail rows without market
data still render.
AssetCandidateDTO.title: AssetCandidateDTO

AssetSearchResponse.description: Top-N candidates for a user query, ordered by market-cap rank.
AssetSearchResponse.title: AssetSearchResponse

BoardEntry.description:
One leaderboard row.

No "regret" / "simulated_size" / "belief_score" surface — the bot
voice rules forbid them. The three reputation numbers we DO
surface are layered views of the same history:

* ``accuracy_pct`` — plain hit rate (the boolean view).
* ``weighted_pnl_pct`` — conviction-weighted signed PnL %
  (the magnitude view). The bot renders this as the primary
  headline; hit rate is the secondary number per the locked
  ``primary_metric = pnl_primary`` choice.

The Bayesian-shrunk sort score that drives the row order is
NOT carried on the wire — it's an internal ranking key, not a
user-facing concept. ``rank`` is the rendered 1-indexed position.
BoardEntry.title: BoardEntry

BoardResponse.description:
``GET /board`` response.

``horizon`` echoes the requested filter so the bot can render the
active filter in the message header (``"Day Traders (≤24h)"`` /
``"Swing Traders (1d-3wk)"`` / ``"Position Traders (>3wk)"``) and
decide which three of the four inline buttons to surface (the
active one is hidden — it's already implicit in the header text).
BoardResponse.title: BoardResponse

text.description: Raw user message; may be empty.
text.title: Text

ClaimDraftResponse.description:
Response of ``POST /claims/draft`` — prefilled fields + asset candidates.

``horizon_seconds`` is the LLM's best parse of the user's horizon
phrase ("3 hours" → 10800, "two weeks" → 1209600). ``None`` when
the LLM's confidence was below the per-field floor or the
extracted value fell outside the API's allowed range — the bot
surfaces the horizon picker in that case. The bot renders the
seconds value via ``humanise_horizon`` (e.g. ``"3 hours"``)
before showing it to the user; this DTO carries the raw number.
ClaimDraftResponse.title: ClaimDraftResponse

ClaimResponse.description:
What ``POST /claims`` returns on success and ``GET /claims/{id}`` returns.

Does **not** surface the v0 simulated conviction-to-dollar mapping
or any internal scoring fields. The user sees their own attested
inputs back, plus the claim id and the resolve date.
ClaimResponse.title: ClaimResponse

CreateInviteRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /invites`` — any onboarded source mints a new code.

Issuance is OPEN: the only authorisation gate is "the caller's
``tg_user_id`` must resolve to an existing ``sources`` row".
Callers without a source row 403 (``not_a_source``) and the bot
turns that into a "send /start first" nudge. Once you're in,
you can mint unlimited codes — no quota at v0 — and every code
is single-use + revokable.

tg_user_id.description: Telegram ID of the caller issuing the invite. The route resolves it to an opaque source_id and checks that the source exists. Unknown callers 403.
tg_user_id.title: Tg User Id

CreateInviteRequest.title: CreateInviteRequest

CreateInviteResponse.description: Response: the freshly minted code, ready to paste.
CreateInviteResponse.title: CreateInviteResponse

ExtractedFieldsDTO.description:
User-attested intent the v0 verifier doesn't score.

Frozen at claim commit per MVP §15 invariant 17. The bot does
**not** surface low-confidence fields on the preview — they live
here for the record.
ExtractedFieldsDTO.title: ExtractedFieldsDTO

HistoryEntry.description:
One row in the user's resolved-call history list.

``observed_return_pct`` is the raw signed move (positive when
the market went up, regardless of the user's direction).

``is_correct`` and ``is_flat`` are both server-side
classifications, derived via ``merlin_core.domain.scoring`` so
the icon set rendered here always matches the live resolution
notification the user already saw. Encoding them on the wire
(rather than recomputing on the bot side) keeps the bot inside
its layer rule — bot is allowed ``merlin_client`` +
``merlin_core.contracts`` only, NOT ``merlin_core.domain``.

Three combinations the bot dispatches on:

* ``is_correct=True`` → won (🎉). ``is_flat`` is always False
  here by construction (``is_correct_call`` returns False on
  flats).
* ``is_correct=False, is_flat=True`` → flat / wash (📝).
* ``is_correct=False, is_flat=False`` → lost (🙂‍↔️).
HistoryEntry.title: HistoryEntry

HistoryResponse.description:
``GET /me/history`` response payload.

Pagination breadcrumbs:

* ``has_more`` — true iff there are more resolved outcomes past
  the current page (within the frozen ``as_of`` window). The bot
  renders the "Show 30 more" button only on this branch.
* ``next_offset`` — offset the next request should pass.
  ``None`` when no more rows are available — pairs with
  ``has_more=False``.
* ``as_of`` — frozen window ceiling. The server stamps this at
  first-page time (caller omits the query param) and echoes the
  caller-supplied value on subsequent pages. The bot **must**
  pass it back on follow-up requests; otherwise an outcome that
  resolves between pages would shift every row downward and the
  "Show 30 more" click would dup the previous page's last row.

Computed server-side as
``has_more = (offset + len(entries) < total_resolved_at_or_before_as_of)``,
``next_offset = offset + limit if has_more else None``.

as_of.description: Frozen window ceiling. Outcomes resolving after this timestamp are excluded from the paginated view so the bot's 'Show 30 more' click never duplicates a boundary row. The bot round-trips this value on follow-up requests.
as_of.title: As Of

HistoryResponse.title: HistoryResponse

MeResponse.description:
``GET /me`` payload — open calls, resolved calls, headline stats.

Headline stats are plain English / plain percent. No "regret",
no "simulated PnL", no version markers.

``accuracy_pct``, ``weighted_pnl_pct``, and ``rank`` are all
``Optional`` because a user with zero resolved calls has no honest
value to report — defaulting to ``0.0`` / ``0`` would tell users
"you're at zero" when the truthful answer is "we haven't checked
anything yet". The bot renders these as "tracking your first
resolutions" rather than a misleading percent.

``weighted_pnl_pct`` is conviction-weighted signed PnL: positive
means the user's calls paid off on aggregate, negative means they
lost. The bot renders it as the primary headline (PnL first, hit
rate as a secondary number) matching the /board layout.
MeResponse.title: MeResponse

OpenCallEntry.description:
One open call on ``/me`` — what the user is waiting on.

``entry_price_usd`` is the snapshot captured when the claim was
submitted (``MarketDataPort.get_price_at(submitted_at)``).
``None`` when CoinGecko was unavailable at submit time (we
never block a bet on market data) or for legacy rows that
predate the column. The bot renders the entry-price line iff
this is set — never invents a placeholder.
OpenCallEntry.title: OpenCallEntry

ParseMetadataDTO.description:
Audit trail of how a claim was constructed.

``raw_user_turns[0]`` is the original freeform message and is
immutable. ``model``, ``model_version``, and ``prompt_hash``
together identify the LLM call exactly so re-runs are auditable.
ParseMetadataDTO.title: ParseMetadataDTO

RedeemInviteRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /invites/redeem``.

Bot sends this after the user pastes their code.
RedeemInviteRequest.title: RedeemInviteRequest

RedeemInviteResponse.description:
Response: opaque ``source_id`` + next-step hint.

``source_id`` is the opaque ``'tg:<sha256>'`` handle from
``merlin_core.domain.source_id.make_source_id`` — a string, never a
UUID (MVP §15 invariant 9). The previous draft of this contract
typed it as ``UUID``; that was wrong and the stub redeem endpoint
only "worked" because it returned a random UUID the bot never
looked at.

``display_name_prompt`` is True iff the source row was just created
and the bot should ask the user for a leaderboard name. False on
idempotent re-redeem (same Telegram user pasting the same code
again — we return their existing source_id).
RedeemInviteResponse.title: RedeemInviteResponse

ResolveAssetRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /assets/resolve``.

The bot sends this after the user picks one candidate. The API
confirms the id against CoinGecko (defence vs. forged ids), then
INSERT-or-fetches the local ``assets`` row.
ResolveAssetRequest.title: ResolveAssetRequest

RevokeInviteRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /invites/revoke`` — admin invalidates an un-redeemed code.

Admin-only. The route checks ``tg_user_id`` against the API's
admin allowlist and 403s non-admins. ``code`` is the exact value
the bot returned from ``POST /invites``.

tg_user_id.description: Telegram ID of the admin revoking the invite. Checked against the API's admin allowlist.
tg_user_id.title: Tg User Id

RevokeInviteRequest.title: RevokeInviteRequest

RevokeInviteResponse.description:
Response: the code that was revoked + the timestamp it was killed.

Returning the code back lets the bot echo the revocation
confirmation without remembering what the admin typed. ``revoked_at``
is the server's wall-clock time at the moment of the UPDATE so the
admin sees the actual recorded value, not an approximation.
RevokeInviteResponse.title: RevokeInviteResponse

SubmitClaimRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /claims`` — atomic commit.

The bot composes this from the preview state (LLM-prefilled fields,
possibly edited by the user, plus the final asset selection).

``tg_user_id`` rides the body for the same reason ``PATCH /me``
needs it: the HMAC bearer authenticates the *service*, not the
per-user identity, so the API has to be told which source is
making the call. Resolved server-side via the
``source_identity`` table — the raw TG id never leaves this
boundary and never ends up on the ``claims`` row itself.
SubmitClaimRequest.title: SubmitClaimRequest

TickerEntry.description:
One ticker's slice of the user's resolved-call portfolio.

Drops the source-level ``MeResponse`` Optional dance — by
construction, every row here represents at least one resolved
call, so the PnL and accuracy are always honest numbers.

``calls_resolved`` is the count that drove the row's shrinkage,
rendered as the trailing chunk ("2 calls") in the bot.
TickerEntry.title: TickerEntry

TickersResponse.description:
``GET /me/tickers`` response payload.

``entries`` is sorted server-side by Bayesian-shrunk PnL (the
same ranking key as ``/board``) with ``calls_resolved`` /
``weighted_pnl_pct`` / ``asset_symbol`` tie-breakers. The bot
renders the list in receive order — no client-side sort.

An empty ``entries`` list signals "cold-start source" (no
resolved calls yet); the bot renders an honest empty-state copy
instead of a misleading zero row.
TickersResponse.title: TickersResponse

UpdateMeRequest.description:
Body of ``PATCH /me``.

Includes ``tg_user_id`` so the API can look up the calling source
via ``source_identity``. The bot's HMAC bearer authenticates the
service, but the API needs the per-user identifier on every
authenticated call (we have no per-user JWT at v0).
UpdateMeRequest.title: UpdateMeRequest

bearerAuth.description: HMAC bearer token for service-to-service requests (MERLIN_API_INTERNAL_TOKEN). Phase 2 adds a JWT scheme for the React frontend.

info.description: The canonical Merlin API. The Telegram bot is one client; future surfaces (React frontend, Pro Dashboard) hit the same flat routes. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
info.title: Merlin API

post.description: The bot calls this after the user picks one of the search candidates. The API confirms the id against CoinGecko (defence vs. forged ids) and materialises the local ``assets`` row. Same coingecko_id → same asset_id (deterministic UUID5).
post.summary: INSERT-or-fetch an asset row by coingecko_id.

get.description: Proxies CoinGecko ``/search`` and returns the top-5 candidates ordered by market-cap rank. Drives the bot's asset-picker on the ``/alpha`` flow (Q-027 lazy asset resolution).
get.summary: Search candidate assets for a freeform query.

get.description: User-facing only: rank, display name, calls resolved, accuracy %, conviction-weighted PnL %, last call date. No belief score, no simulated dollar PnL, no version markers. Sort order is internal (Bayesian-shrunk PnL); the bot renders PnL as the primary headline with hit rate as a secondary number.

parameters.description: Four-mode horizon filter the bot surfaces as 'Day Traders' (<=24h), 'Swing Traders' (1d-3wk), 'Position Traders' (>3wk), and 'All'. Boundaries are HORIZON_DAY_TRADER_MAX_SECONDS and HORIZON_SWING_TRADER_MAX_SECONDS in merlin_core.contracts.horizons. 'all' reads the pre-aggregated snapshot table; 'day' / 'swing' / 'position' recompute on-the-fly so the snapshot table stays horizon-agnostic.
parameters.name: horizon

schema.description: Four-mode horizon filter the bot surfaces as 'Day Traders' (<=24h), 'Swing Traders' (1d-3wk), 'Position Traders' (>3wk), and 'All'. Boundaries are HORIZON_DAY_TRADER_MAX_SECONDS and HORIZON_SWING_TRADER_MAX_SECONDS in merlin_core.contracts.horizons. 'all' reads the pre-aggregated snapshot table; 'day' / 'swing' / 'position' recompute on-the-fly so the snapshot table stays horizon-agnostic.
schema.title: Horizon

get.summary: Leaderboard — top-N sources ranked by conviction-weighted PnL.

post.description: Persists the ``claims`` row and enqueues the RQ resolution job inside one request. ``tg_user_id`` is resolved to a ``source_id`` via the ``source_identity`` table; unknown users 404 (onboard via ``/invites/redeem`` or ``/sources/admin_bootstrap`` first). Returns the persisted claim with its resolve date.

Stateless. One LLM call, optionally one CoinGecko ``/search`` call. Returns a prefilled draft for the bot to render on its preview. On any LLM failure, returns 503 — the bot then falls back to the button form.

503.description: LLM unavailable; bot should fall back to the button flow.

get.description: Returns the user-visible shape of a claim: verbatim thesis, resolve date, outcome if resolved. No internal scoring fields.
Cheap check used by Fly's restart healthcheck. No DB or Redis required.

post.description: Generates a URL-safe ~11-character code and stores it with an expiry. Open to any caller whose ``tg_user_id`` resolves to an existing ``sources`` row (i.e. they've completed onboarding via ``/invites/redeem`` or ``admin_bootstrap``). Callers without a source row 403 with ``not_a_source`` — the bot renders a 'send /start first' nudge on that path.
post.summary: Issue a new invite code (open to any onboarded source).

post.description: Single transaction: validate invite, INSERT ``sources`` (zeroed Admiralty: ``reliability='F'``, ``credibility=6``), INSERT ``source_identity``, UPDATE ``invites`` redeemed. Returns the new ``source_id`` and a hint to prompt for display name. Unknown / expired / already-redeemed codes 404.
post.summary: Redeem an invite code (atomic — INSERT sources + UPDATE invites).

post.description: Marks the invite as revoked so future ``POST /invites/redeem`` calls 404 against it. Atomic — two simultaneous revoke calls for the same code can never both succeed. Returns 404 if the code is unknown, already redeemed, or already revoked (the three indistinguishable terminal states from a revoke-caller's perspective). Caller must be a Telegram admin (``TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_IDS``); non-admin callers 403.

get.description: User-visible only: open calls (asset + direction + resolve date), recent resolved calls with plain-percent returns, accuracy. ``tg_user_id`` query param resolves the caller via the ``source_identity`` table (same convention as ``PATCH /me``). 404s if the caller hasn't been onboarded yet.

parameters.description: Caller's raw Telegram user id. The HMAC bearer authenticates the service, not the per-user identity, so the API needs the TG id on every authenticated call (we have no per-user JWT at v0). Same convention as ``PATCH /me``.
parameters.name: tg_user_id

schema.description: Caller's raw Telegram user id. The HMAC bearer authenticates the service, not the per-user identity, so the API needs the TG id on every authenticated call (we have no per-user JWT at v0). Same convention as ``PATCH /me``.
schema.title: Tg User Id

get.summary: Current source's open + resolved calls and headline stats.

patch.description: Idempotent — calling with the same name is a no-op. The display name has a 40-character soft cap; the bot trims user input before sending. 404s if the caller's ``tg_user_id`` has no source row yet. On the first-ever display-name set for an invited user, sends the inviter a notification — fired exactly once per invitee, gated on the previous ``display_name`` being NULL so a later rename does not re-notify.
patch.summary: Set the display name shown on the leaderboard.

get.description: Paginated via ``limit`` / ``offset`` with a frozen ``as_of`` window ceiling. Default page size is 30, matching the bot's "Show 30 more" inline button. The first page omits ``as_of`` and the server stamps it with the request's wall-clock UTC time; the response echoes the value back, and the bot must round-trip it on subsequent pages so a new outcome landing mid-session can't shift already-paged rows down into the next page (which would dup the boundary row on the next click). The response also carries ``has_more`` + ``next_offset`` so the bot can render the button without keeping its own count. 404s if the caller has no source row yet.

parameters.description: Caller's raw Telegram user id. Same identity-lookup convention as ``GET /me``.

schema.title: Tg User Id

parameters.description: Maximum rows to return in this page. Defaults to 30 — one bot page. Capped at 100 so a misbehaving client can't drain the database in one request.
parameters.name: limit

schema.description: Maximum rows to return in this page. Defaults to 30 — one bot page. Capped at 100 so a misbehaving client can't drain the database in one request.

Subsequent pages must round-trip the same value to avoid pagination drift when a new outcome resolves mid-session.

schema.title: As Of

get.summary: The caller's resolved calls, newest first.

get.description: User-facing only: ticker, conviction-weighted PnL %, hit rate %, resolved-call count. Sorted server-side by the same Bayesian-shrunk score the leaderboard uses, so single-bet tickers with outsized PnL never out-rank consistent multi-bet tickers. Cold-start tickers (no resolved calls) are filtered out — every row has at least one resolved bet. 404s if the caller has no source row yet.
